https://www.americanthinker.com/blog/202.text: Culture > Holocaust Link copied The Martin-Springer Institute: Another Holocaust institute falls to the antisemitic left Founded to prevent a future Holocaust, the MSI now attacks Israel, siding with those who dream of Israel’s destruction. Andrea Widburg | August 6, 2026 Ever since a 2012 visit to the Anne Frank House in Amsterdam, I’ve known that the left has been very busy reworking the Holocaust so that it’s not about a unique evil visited upon the Jewish people, but is just shorthand for deaths in the Third World and Middle East (except, of course, for Jewish deaths). It’s not just the Anne Frank House. Other organizations once dedicated to Anne Frank have become actively antisemitic . It seems that the same is slowly happening to the Martin-Springer Institute (“MSI”) at Northern Arizona University in Flagstaff (“NAU”) The MSI reflects the experiences of Doris Szpringer Martin, a Polish Jew who, at 12, ended up in Auschwitz, before being shifted to Ludwigsdorf, a women’s forced-labor camp. She and her immediate family survived the war and immigrated to America, where she met her husband, Ralph Martin. Hoping to prevent another Holocaust from ever occurring, in 2000 the Martins established the MSI at NAU, along with another one at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Israel. It was not intended to be a Holocaust memorial, looking backward, but was meant to prevent a future Holocaust by ending mindsets that dehumanized some people, that created a hierarchy of worthy versus unworthy people, or that otherwise set the stage for demanding the eradication of a specific set of people. To that end, MSI’s mission is to attend “to the experiences of the Holocaust in order to relate them to today’s concerns, crises, and conflicts,” while emphasizing the values of moral courage, empathy, resilience, reconciliation, justice, and tolerance. While the MSI still does a lot of Holocaust related work, it’s suffered institutional capture, so that its focus has drifted far, far left. Now, in addition to reminding people of the Holocaust so they can steer away from deadly ethnic and ideological hatreds, it also obsesses about : Israeli treatment of Palestinians and Bedouins. American treatment of Native Americans. Government-sanctioned torture. Racism and anti-Black violence. Immigration policy and refugees. Colonialism. Disappearances in Mexico. Threats to democracy. That’s pure leftist lingo, and as you have noted, many of those obsessions have a decidedly anti-white, anti-Western, and, ironically given how Doris Spinger’s Holocaust experience created the MSI, antisemitic tone. The following speakers, all from this year, show the direction of the MSI. On February 17, the MSI sponsored “ An Evening with the Pulitzer Prize Winning Author of The Sympathizer: Viet Thanh Nguyen .” That sounds very cool, but should a Holocaust institute be sponsoring someone who obsessively accuses Israel of genocide, supports BDS and culturally boycotting Israel, and frames the conflict in Israel through a “settler colonialism” lens (which ignores that Jews have been there for over 3,000 years, and today’s “Palestinians” for barely 200 )? (See, e.g., here , here , and here .) On March 26, the MSI hosted Bridget Conley, who once worked as the Research Director for the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum’s Committee on Conscience, and is now a World Peace Foundation & Research Professor from Tufts University. Conley spoke about “ The Indispensability of Gender: Starvation in Contemporary Contexts. ” It’s likely that her speech reflected her boundless hostility to Israel , which she describes as carrying out a “campaign of atrocities” against civilians, including using starvation as a weapon. And on April 8, the MSI also hosted Tylor Brand, from the Department of Near & Middle Eastern Studies at Trinity College in Dublin (located in what is truly a nation that is a hotbed of stupid antisemitism ), to speak about “ Famine and Induced Starvation During War and Colonial Suppression: Middle East and North Africa .” There doesn’t seem to be a publicly available transcript of the talk, but it just might have reflected his claim that there’s a “manmade famine Israel has imposed on Gaza.” Apparently, both Conley and Brand missed reports about Israel’s sending hundreds of tons of food to enemy civilians, as well as the documented fact that Hamas stole the food (something even the UN grudgingly admitted on one occasion). They also seem to have missed these videos out of Gaza: Abundance of fresh food in Rafah, Gaza Strip. Markets are bursting with food including; fresh fruit, vegetables, spices, bagels and iced tea pic.twitter.com/D2f5brZr9E Abundance of food on display at Deir al-Balah market in Gaza including; cereals, avocados and bananas. pic.twitter.com/DJ0U7KgkXD Grocery store in Gaza appears fully stocked with food including chocolate and pretzels. pic.twitter.com/camIsliWa1 These are all in the last 48 hours from Gaza City, @SkyNews Gazans, posting on their own social media accounts. Stacked market shelves of food in Gaza City, sweets and snacks, cafés open for business, freshly made pizzas etc. Confused? You should be. https://t.co/nIMX3MJNti pic.twitter.com/62hhYtYH4X Maybe the famine is because the Gazans are eating too much junk food? What’s more likely is that Hamas and other war profiteers ensured that they were well-fed, while Gazans and, especially, Israeli hostages were not. The one thing that never came out of Gaza was pictures like these , of the Bergen-Belsen prisoners whom the Allies arrived too late to save from disease and starvation (content warning). At bottom, all of these speakers are targeting and dehumanizing Israel and Israelis. By doing so, they provide fuel for the malevolent, genocidal antisemitism that has spread from the Muslims of the Middle East across the West. John O’Sullivan famously said that “any organization or enterprise that is not expressly right-wing will become left-wing over time.” Nowhere has that happened more grotesquely than in institutions originally dedicated to the Holocaust. What’s taking place at the Martin-Springer Institute is Exhibit A in the catastrophic leftist, antisemitic capture of the Holocaust, one that is teeing the world up for another organized attempt to erase Jews from the face of the earth. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5y4.text: Figure caption, Watch: What we know about the fatal Philippines ferry fire By Virma Simonette Rivera ,Â Reporting from Manila Â and Â Koh Ewe Published 52 minutes ago Passengers on board a ferry to the Philippines' Palawan province were jolted into chaos on Wednesday night, when a fire broke out on the vessel. Frantic cries pierced the night sky as hot air filled the boat, recalls Roland Lerma, one of more than 100 passengers aboard the MV June Aster. Five people have died and 86 people are missing after the fire, which, in a country where shipping accidents are not uncommon, could become one of the deadliest maritime disasters the Philippines has seen. Families are anxiously awaiting news about their loved ones on board, while survivors like Lerma are coming to terms with their harrowing escape. Speaking to the BBC from a hospital in Coron, Lerma recalled that as the fire spread and he scrambled to get off the burning boat, he slipped and fell. "When I was on the floor, people were trampling me," said the 30-year-old. He started crawling until he could find his footing again, before leaping off the vessel into the sea. He said he saw children who had also jumped in the water, though he could not make out their faces in the dark. "When I hit the water, I ditched all my possessions - the clothes I was wearing, phones, bags - so that I could float," he said. Lerma said he floated on his back for about two hours before rescuers arrived and pulled him and other survivors out of the water. "It was cold. If the rescue had been delayed, I would have definitely died last night," he said. Image source, Philippine Coast Guard via EPA/Shutterstock Image caption, Survivors have been rescued from a deadly ferry fire near a holiday spot in the Philippines', though dozens remain missing Lerma, who works in construction, is from Leyte province. He had travelled to the capital Manila with five of his neighbours, where they boarded the ferry to bring them to work at Coron, a popular tourist spot in Palawan province. According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the MV June Aster departed Manila's Port of Baseco on Tuesday night at 20:13 local time (12:13 GMT) and was scheduled to arrive at the Coron port at 18:00 on Wednesday. But the ferry caught fire just 1.2 nautical miles (2.2km) off the coast of Coron's Marcilla village. The fire was first reported at 18:45 local time on Wednesday night by a staff member of Atienza Shipping Lines, which owns the boat, the Coast Guard said. The company said in a statement on Thursday that it was co-operating fully with authorities and expressed "profound sadness" about the fire. Authorities say a survivor had told them the flames had started in the cargo hold after a loud explosion. The ship had been carrying several motorcycles, an electric car, a forklift, a pick-up van and other goods, the Philippine Coast Guard said. As the journey was expected to take more than 20 hours, passengers had slept on bunk beds onboard overnight. Lerma said that two Chileans - a couple who looked like they were in their late 20s or early 30s - had slept in the beds next to his. Authorities have since confirmed that two Chilean nationals were among the 43 people rescued. Lerma and two of his neighbours are now in a hospital in Coron. Another person in their group has been taken to a bigger hospital in the neighbouring island of Culion, while two others remain missing, Lerma says. "I have a couple of bruises and my chest is still hurting," Lerma said. "Last night, I had a hard time breathing. But I am okay now." Image source, Roland Lerma Image caption, Roland Lerma (right) jumped into the sea as the ferry went up in flames Image source, Philippine Coast Guard via Getty Images Image caption, The fire on the MV June Aster has not gone out, authorities say Search and rescue operations are ongoing, though authorities say the fire on the MV June Aster has still not been put out and there was visible smoke from the ferry. A spokesperson for the Philippine Coast Guard said in a local television interview many of the survivors "are still in shock". Meanwhile, families of the ferry's missing passengers are enduring an agonising wait. Anelyn Magbanua told the BBC that her husband Marlon was on the ferry. He was returning to Coron after visiting Manila to see two of their children who are studying at the capital. "He spent a couple of days there. He even sent me their pictures," she said. She last heard from him while the ferry was passing through a village about two hours from the port in Coron. Magbanua and her two-year-old son had gone to bed early on Wednesday night expecting Marlon to be home soon. But she was woken up later that night by a relative who informed her that her husband's ferry had caught fire. On Thursday she rushed to the hospital when she heard there was a chance her husband might be one of the rescued survivors there. But officials have since told her that Marlon remains unaccounted for. "My two-year-old son and I are outside the hospital as we speak. We have nothing but ourselves," she told the BBC over the phone. "I can't describe what I am feeling right now. I have been crying and praying since last night." https://hvg.hu/itthon/20261111_kiemelt-b.text: A legújabb Magyar Közlöny szerint pedig a Liszt Ferenc Nemzetközi Repülőtér közúti elérhetőségének javításnál továbbra is marad ez a minősítés. A szerda este megjelent rendelet , amellyel a kormány kiemelt beruházássá nyilvánítja a 71-es számú Budapest–Vácrátót–Vác vasútvonal előkészítéséhez és megvalósításához szükséges beruházásokat. A hivatalos lapban több mint 200 oldalon, tengelypont-koordináták és helyrajzi számok szeriunt felsorolt ingatlanok és a belőlük a telekalakítási eljárásban hozott döntés véglegessé válását követően kialakított ingatlanok tekintetében változtatási tilalom, valamint telekalakítási és építési tilalom nem alkalmazható. Kiemelt beruházás esetén a kormány által meghatározott beépítés szabályokat és egyedi építési követelményeket kell figyelembe venni, semmilyen ezekkel ellentétes országos és helyi jogszabályt, például területrendezési és településrendezési tervet nem kell alkalmazni. Egyebek közt a zöldfelület megengedett legkisebb mértéke 0 százalék, támfalra vonatkozó magassági és kialakítási megkötés nincs, a támfal merevítését szolgáló szerkezet a terepszint alatt a szükséges mélységben közterület alá nyúlhat, az egyébként előírt számú parkolóhelyet nem kell kialakítani. Az is a szokásos záradék, hogy mindez ugyan csütörtöktől hatályos, de a folyamatban lévő ügyekre is alkalmazni kell. Egy ugyancsak most közzé tett határozatban a kormány megállapítja, hogy a Budapest Liszt Ferenc Nemzetközi Repülőtér közúti elérhetőségének javítása továbbra is kiemelt jelentőségű beruházás, de az előző kormány erről szóló határozatát visszavonja. Felhívja a közlekedési és beruházási minisztert, hogy gondoskodjon a projekt megvalósításához szükséges, megkezdett területszerzési és terület-előkészítési feladatok végrehajtásának folytatásáról és folyamatos ellátásáról, a kiviteli tervek rendelkezésre állását követően a kivitelező kiválasztására irányuló feltételes közbeszerzési eljárást indítsa meg és folytassa le. Az idén fel nem használt és a központi költségvetés javára elvont forrás összegének figyelembevételével a pénzügyminiszter jövőre legfeljebb 8 milliárd, 2028-ban 16 milliárd forint forrásra tegyen javaslatot. Mivel a kormány egyetért a fővárosi (helyi) és elővárosi személyszállítási közszolgáltatások integrált és hatékonyabb ellátása érdekében a Fővárosi Közfejlesztések Tanácsának határozatában foglalt célokkal és javaslatokkal, az is Vitézy Dávid feladata, hogy a Fővárosi Önkormányzattal és az új OKK Országos Közlekedési Központ Zrt.-vel kösse meg a közös közlekedésszervező létrehozásáról szóló megrendelői együttműködési megállapodást, és tegye meg a szükséges intézkedéseket annak érdekében, hogy az OKK a BKK zártkörű alaptőke-emelése keretében kibocsátott új részvények névértéken történő átvételével 50%-os tulajdonrészt szerezzen a BKK-ban. A bíróság egy hónapra elrendelte Orbán Áron letartóztatását, ott voltunk, amikor ezt követően rendőrautóban vitték el a Fővárosi Törvényszékről.

Photograph: Zsolt Szigetváry/EPA Hungary University hounded out of Hungary by Orbán reaches out to new government Prospect of partial return to Budapest by Central European University suggests confidence in Hungary’s future Jennifer Rankin in Brussels Sat 14 Nov 2026 00.00 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 00.02 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A university that Viktor Orbán tried to chase out of Hungary is open to expanding its presence in Budapest, in a mark of confidence in the country’s democratic future. Carsten Q Schneider, the interim president and rector of Central European University (CEU), said it was interested in increasing its programmes in Budapest, as long as this did not damage the student experience. So far the CEU has not held formal talks with Hungary’s new government, which has promised to restore academic freedom, “but our hand is reaching out, their hand is reaching out – it is just that they have many things to do ”, the academic told the Guardian. The CEU relocated its main activities to Vienna from Budapest in 2019, after pressure from the previous government led by Orbán. But the outlook changed when Péter Magyar won a landslide victory in April pledging to root out corruption and reform the state . The CEU, founded by Hungarian-American financier and philanthropist George Soros in 1991 to entrench democratic change in the region, was forced to cease awarding degrees in Budapest in response to a law widely seen as targeting the institution. The EU’s highest court struck down Hungary’s “Lex CEU” in 2020 , finding that it violated the EU charter of fundamental rights, but the verdict came too late for the university. The CEU retains 312 staff in Budapest, mostly administrative, but the majority, 476, and all its teaching, are in Vienna. View image in fullscreen CEU’s main building in Budapest, pictured in 2018. Photograph: Bernadett Szabó/Reuters Schneider said upgrading the status of the CEU, which is privately funded, in Budapest would be “a symbol for academic freedom [and] of resilience” but depended on goodwill and funding independent of the Hungarian government. He said a decision on its future in Hungary would be taken by the CEU’s 13-member board, whose members include Soros and his son, Alexander Soros. “We don’t want special treatment,” Schneider said. ‘“We are a great asset, so let’s work out something.” But the CEU, which he said was “thriving tremendously” in Vienna, does not plan a wholesale return to Budapest. Any change would have to ensure the quality of the student experience, for instance, assuring that students would be able to combine courses, say in economics and history, without having to travel the 200km-plus distance between the two cities. Focused on social sciences, law and humanities, the CEU has more than 1,400 students from 103 countries, mostly doing master’s and PhD programmes. According to Schneider, for the first time in the CEU’s 25-year history, students from the US now make up the largest cohort of master’s students (10%). The CEU has seen an increase in US applicants since Donald Trump returned to the White House and launched a sweeping campaign against elite universities , including slashing federal funding and seeking to exert control over internal policies . The CEU rector has had informal talks with US academics on how to maintain academic freedom under pressure from rightwing populists. He described his message as: “Don’t be naive for a second. These people have a plan, so it’s not by accident that they attack universities. They want to have cultural hegemony.” He added, however, that Trump and allied movements, such as Germany’s Alternative für Deutschland, have identified “real problems”, such as in the US how universities have entrenched “a reproduction of elites” When coming under political pressure, he said universities needed “to look for allies”, among other academic institutions, students, alumni and parents. So he knows something.” He added: “The people and skills that you need to bring a non-democratic regime down are not the same and sometimes the opposite of what it takes to establish a democracy. So the question now is whether he [Magyar] has the skills to basically reinvent liberal democracy for the 21st century.” Schneider said Hungary could be the world’s first “post-illiberal democracy” – a model for democratic restoration, just as Orbán inspired rightwing populists around the world. But he also raised doubts about this thesis, saying there were questions about how Magyar and his Tisza party might develop in the context of Hungary’s “very difficult economic situation”. The test would be, he suggested, when Magyar faces losing support and, eventually, defeat at the ballot box. “So what happens when he loses support and then cracks in his movement appear? Will he be the visionary leader who manages … to establish a three, four, five-party system, where people compete?
